html:
The langi are terraced stone tombs at Lapaha, on the lagoon of Tongatapu, where the sacred kings called the Tuʻi Tonga were buried from about the 13th century. Their faced coral blocks were cut and hauled from the coast.

Lapaha was the seat of the Tuʻi Tonga, whose canoes and marriage ties linked Tonga with Samoa, Fiji and Wallis. Nearby stands the trilithon of Haʻamonga ʻa Maui.

Over time the sacred line lost real power to other chiefly titles. The last Tuʻi Tonga died in 1865, after George Tupou I had united Tonga under a new royal house.
